decisions.reason: The degree-two circle immersion has equal tangent lines at coincident branches, so orientation alone supplies no transverse sign. Added self-transversality explicitly both to complementary-sheet and sign claims. The normal quotient of the target diagonal is the difference of tangent blocks; surjectivity gives complementary planes in dimension 2m. Swapping m-blocks has determinant (-1)^(m*m), so the even/odd sign convention and branch-pair versus image distinction remain valid.

The coordinate subtori and diagonal in T^4 give one triple image and three transverse unordered pairs, whose parity equals the image count. Replaced the false necessary condition by the valid triple-free termwise identification, allowing accidental equality with triples. Finiteness follows from compactness away from a local-injectivity diagonal neighbourhood and invertibility of the difference derivative. Also supplied the chosen-path label calculation directly: conjugating the Whitney loop by a whisker is invertible, and common left multiplication preserves equality; this needs only paths, not the closed embedded sheets assumed in the cited geometric label lemma.

Clause 2 and L5 asserted an oriented sign without orientations. The disk existence and standard model are valid without orientations; qualified only the sign conclusion and its proof by orientations of M,X and induced disk orientations. Self-transversality holds at every pair in the disjoint source charts, so the transverse-intersection theorem isolates their zero-dimensional intersection after shrinking at r. Local embeddings, compact coordinate disks and the graph-straightening map supply the geometric conclusions.

The constant full-product map to (0,0) for S^1 into R^3 is equivariant but sends every off-diagonal pair to the diagonal. Qualified the restriction claim by isovariance, whose defining preimage equality gives precisely the needed avoidance. Consulted cached Wall PDF /tmp/b16-wall.pdf, printed pp.184-192: the fixed-set definition, Lemma 6.4.1, Theorem 6.4.8 and the published outline of 6.4.9; its stated dimension ranges match the recorded clauses. Consulted Skopenkov section 5, pp.30-32, for the Gauss map and Theorem 5.4. The remark remains explicitly unproved; no complete independent proof of the classification is claimed. Its heading is Remark, so no Statement/Definition changed.

The finite-dimensional perturbation proof is sound: immersion charts exclude near-diagonal coincidences uniformly; independent bump translations make pair/triple evaluations submersions; negative triple dimension excludes triples; invertible pair derivatives and a compact complement give a swap-compatible persistence bijection and preserve nonzero determinant signs. Confirmed the required missing ambient-compactness citation as nonfatal and added it in F6/deps, with product and closed-subspace compactness suppliers. Formed the cover from all witness neighbourhoods before choosing finite witnesses, preserving the declared countable-choice boundary. The Statement is unchanged.

Confirmed the missing mandatory ambient-compactness citation as a nonfatal dependency-citation defect. Added it to F4/deps and made step 1.2 use all injectivity neighbourhoods before extracting finitely many, so A1's no-additional-choice claim is accurate. In four-space the isolated ordered pairs are closed in a compact complement of a diagonal neighbourhood, hence finite; multiple pairs may share their image. In five-space the negative expected dimension gives injectivity, and compact source gives properness, yielding an embedding. The Example interface is unchanged.

For M=[0,1] and the constant embedding into R, the track is the square and has genuine corners. Replaced the incorrect endpoint submanifold-with-boundary assertion by the existing isotopy definition's product-corner coordinate-extension convention, retaining all compact sources. In step 2.2 extended source coordinates across source boundary faces as well as time endpoints before using the invertible block map (p(F(u,t)),t). Its local inverse supplies smooth track coordinates and smooth velocity up to each face/corner. Injectivity, compact-to-Hausdorff topology, horizontal differentiation and boundary-stratum tangency remain valid; no neatness is asserted.

L4 misstated the canonical time-first domain as N×I. This is a nonfatal notation/interface citation defect: the constructed space-first map has the right fibres and becomes the defined field by a smooth factor swap. Added H:I×N→TN, H(t,y)=G(y,t), in the Statement, L4 and step 3.1 while preserving every slice G_t. Compact support follows from the compact projection of supp rho, which is contained in the relatively compact track neighbourhood. The endpoint cutoff equals one wherever the original velocity can be nonzero, so matching and vanishing conclusions remain correct.

The path F(*,t)=t cannot have a stationary ambient extension at the endpoints, so clause 4's retention of that conclusion was false. Explicitly omitted both endpoint constancy and endpoint stationarity in clause 4. Preserved the complements corollary's compact-source scope by allowing boundary in clause 1 and clause 4: the now-corrected track graph inverse, neighbourhood velocity extension and finite product-chart cutoffs already have that scope, and the target flow argument is unaffected. Updated F2 and L6 to carry product-corner coordinate conventions and L2 to use the time-first field representative. ODE uniqueness proves matching, compact spatial support gives global flow, and tangency or interior support gives clause 3; relative open-track inversion proves clause 2.

The frozen extension supplier required boundaryless M, while this corollary allowed a compact source with boundary, so the original L1/step 1.1 invocation was outside the supplied hypotheses (fatal dependency-citation defect). The assigned theorem has now been proved with the full compact-source scope using its corner-valid velocity, extension and cutoff suppliers. Made that boundary permission explicit in L1 and step 1.1 without narrowing the corollary Statement. The time-one ambient diffeomorphism identifies the images and their open complements; composing any extension embedding with it preserves injectivity, immersion and the image topology.

The Euclidean half-plane example F(x,t)=(x,t) has unit speed but carries boundary into interior, so no ambient diffeomorphism can realize it: a diffeomorphism preserves the boundary stratum. Added the exact boundary/interior alternatives of Hirsch Theorem 1.6 and the separate open-track condition of Theorem 1.7, distinguishing their hypotheses. Consulted cached /tmp/batch19-hirsch.pdf, printed pp.178-181, including the boundary-tangent field definition, the complete-metric flow argument and Theorems 1.3/1.4/1.6/1.7 (the last two leave proofs to the reader). Consulted UCR handout printed pp.2-4 for the knot-to-infinity counterexample and complement-group obstruction. This remains a recorded Remark, with no Statement/Definition interface change.
